text: A Forth REPL. The interpreter says `ok` as soon as it starts. Type `: sq dup * ;` and press Enter; it answers `ok` again. Then `7 sq .` prints `49 ` in front of the next `ok`. `bye` returns to the shell.

Everything Forth owns lives in the bank window of tape 0: data stack at 0x4000, return stack at 0x4080, dictionary from 0x4100, names at 0x4400, threaded code from 0x4800. Nothing above 0x5900 is touched unless you store there with `!`.
Define a word and watch cells appear at 0x4800. A cell below 100 is a primitive id; a cell of 100 or more calls the word whose body starts at that offset minus 100.
Every keystroke arrives through the CONIN syscall. When nothing is queued the machine parks in IDLE and wakes on the next byte you type; the prompt is written through CONOUT.
Compare head travel for `words`, which walks the whole name table, with `dup`, which touches two stack cells next to each other.
To extend the language, add a name to the boot string in forth.c and a matching branch in prim(), then recompile from this editor and run it again.
